Dear [Mr Innes](../persons.html#744)
Thank you. [Mr Smith](../persons.html#1344) generously sends me £50 in January [£40](../others.html#160) for my editorship and £10 for the [subeditor](../persons.html#512).

The other payments this month are for
Angela,
Miss [Alice Weber](../persons.html#1483)
10 Randolph Road
Maida Hill
The Georgian Princess
[Miss Dempster](../persons.html#434)
Villa Rey
Cannes
(She is author of Vera and rather a great gun, so should have full pay)
Papers on Rome
The Rev [Wm Jeffreys Hills](../persons.html#697)
Beaufort Road
Winchester
St Paul
Miss [Selina Gaye](../persons.html#552)
14 Artesian Road
Bayswater
Miracle Plays
[Alfred Pollard](../persons.html#1185) Esq
British Museum
Old World Legend
[Mrs Keir Moilliet](../persons.html#804)
Abbot’s Legh
Malvern
I think I have pretty well arranged about the Cambridge Literature papers. [Miss Knatchbull Hugesson](../persons.html#820) ([Lord Brabourne](../persons.html#819)’s daughter) will write them, and find a questioner and critic to work in concert with, and we will have the two prizes as you propose.[^1] The remaining question is shall this £5 come out of the fees for entering for the examination in the Society - or will you pay it, and let the whole sum go to the critic, who will most likely be some [Newnham](../others.html#7) lady to whom some remuneration would be an object. I am glad to have Miss K H, as her father is sure to take interest in her work

Yours truly

C M Yonge

[^1]: The June 1888 issue of MP included, p. 595, an announcement that \'On July 1st a series of Papers on English Literature will be commenced by the Hon.

Eva Knatchbull-Hugessen, intended to assist in preparation for that branch of the Cambridge Higher Local Examination for Women, to be held in June 1889.

Questions will be set after each Paper by Miss Mackenzie, late scholar of Newnham College Cambridge\'.
